key_insight: The paper studies how D-gun sprayed WC-12Co and Al2O3-13TiO2 coatings behave tribologically, and uses machine learning to predict wear and friction performance.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for selecting and optimizing thermal-sprayed protective coatings in wear-critical machinery, tooling, and surface-engineering applications.
method: Prepared and tested WC-12Co and Al2O3-13TiO2 detonation-sprayed coatings
Evaluated tribological behavior through wear and friction measurements
Built machine learning models to assist prediction of coating performance
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a journal article in Journal of Thermal Spray Technology, but it does not provide dataset size, model metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Prediction quality may depend strongly on the coating/process variables and test conditions, so the model may need careful validation before use on new spray settings.
paper_title: Tribological Performance and Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Wear and Friction in D-Gun Sprayed WC-12Co and Al2O3-13TiO2 Coatings
